search.recordChats: Record chats with {assistant} and the actions they take

appearance.panelsHelp: Drag a panel by its header, or right-click its header or its icon, to move it to the left, the right or the bottom. Where you put things is remembered on this computer.
appearance.alreadyDefault: Everything is already where it starts.
appearance.terminalHelp: The type size in a coding agent's console. You can also change it from the console's own header, with Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus / Ctrl+0, or by holding Ctrl and scrolling over the terminal.
appearance.tourHelp: You can still launch the tour or checklist anytime from the Help menu or the command palette.
appearance.showReleaseNotes: Show release notes after an update
appearance.gpuHelp: Draws the app using your graphics card, which is faster and is the right choice for almost everyone. Turn this off only if the app crashes on startup, shows blank or corrupted panels, or flickers. Those are usually signs of a graphics driver problem, and software rendering avoids it at some cost in speed.
appearance.gpuAutoDisabled: SnoutData Studio turned this off for you because your graphics card kept crashing, which was making the app close unexpectedly. Updating your graphics driver usually fixes it. You can turn it back on here.
appearance.gpuRestart: Restart SnoutData Studio for this to take effect.

editor.autoLimit: Auto-append LIMIT to a bare SELECT
editor.transcribe: Auto-translate unsupported SQL to a MongoDB pipeline with {assistant}
editor.transcribeHelp: On document connections (MongoDB), when a query is too complex for the built-in translator, use AI without asking each time. Every AI call uses your budget. Off by default, so the first such query asks first. Or write native pipelines in the Pipeline tab.
editor.confirmOnProd: Confirm destructive statements on prod connections
editor.allowGridActionsHint: (edit value, copy, copy row) on prod connections
editor.resolveFk: Resolve foreign-key ids to inline labels in the grid
editor.resolveFkHelp: Fires a small lookup per FK column over the visible rows. The hover/right-click peek card stays available either way.
editor.preflightScan: Warn before a query the planner expects to scan a huge number of rows
editor.preflightHelp: Runs one cheap EXPLAIN before a SELECT (on prod/tunnelled connections too, where a runaway scan hurts most). The same plan powers the index/scan advice, so there's no second round-trip.
editor.warnSlow: Warn a running query is slow after (ms)
editor.adviseAfter: Advise on index/scans after a query takes (ms)
editor.thresholdsHelp: Set the two thresholds to 0 to turn off the long-running warning or the post-run index advice.
editor.autoConnect: Connect automatically when picking a connection from a dropdown
editor.autoConnectHelp: When off, the dropdowns only select; connect from the sidebar.
editor.reconnect: Reopen connections that were open last launch
editor.reconnectHelp: Only non-prod connections reopen; prod always needs a manual connect.

connections.intro: Every database this app can reach, the same list as the sidebar's. Connect, edit or remove one here; the passwords stay in this computer's keychain.
connections.introWeak: Every database this app can reach, the same list as the sidebar's. Connect, edit or remove one here; the passwords stay on this computer.
connections.weakSecrets: This computer has no password vault (keyring), so passwords are saved in a file only your user account can read. Install one, such as GNOME Keyring, and restart Studio to keep them in a vault.
connections.empty: No connections yet. Add one to browse its tables and query it.

network.intro: How SnoutData Studio connects to the internet for sign-in, AI, and updates. The default follows your system proxy, like your browser. Change this only if you're on a company network that needs a specific proxy or proxy sign-in (for example Zscaler or a corporate firewall).
network.modeSystemHint: Resolve the OS proxy (PAC/WPAD/manual) the same way your browser does. Recommended.
network.modeDirectHint: Connect straight out, ignoring any system proxy.
network.modeManualHint: Point the app at a specific PAC file or proxy server.
network.pacHelp: If you have a PAC URL, use it. Otherwise leave it blank and set a proxy server below.
network.signInHelp: Only if your proxy asks for a username and password. Windows/Kerberos single sign-on is handled automatically and needs nothing here. Kept {place}.
network.passwordHelp: A password is saved. Leave blank to keep it, or clear the field and save to remove it.
network.windowsHelp: Your proxy can always use your Windows/Kerberos sign-in. Other servers can only if they are listed here, and nothing receives your Kerberos ticket unless it is listed under delegation. Leave both blank unless your IT team asks. Changes apply the next time SnoutData Studio starts.
network.authServers: Servers allowed to use your Windows sign-in
network.delegateServers: Servers your Kerberos ticket may be delegated to
network.hostsHelp: Comma separated host names. A leading `*.` covers a domain; a bare `*` is not accepted.
network.resolvedTitle: What Chromium resolves for a sample request
network.reachableHelp: "Reachable" means the app got a response from the host. A failure here with a code like `net::ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED` tells you (or your IT team) what to fix.

shortcuts.intro: Click a shortcut, then press the new key combination. Esc to cancel, Backspace to reset.
shortcuts.overridesTitle: These keys also trigger a built-in: {name}. Your binding wins, but disables it.

commands.libyHelp: {assistant}: help with what I am doing

knowledge.intro: Durable facts you teach the assistant so it stops getting the same domain quirks wrong. **General** rules apply to every database (e.g. “always use CTEs”); pick a specific database for facts about its tables. These notes are sent to {assistant} with your prompts, just like your schema is.
knowledge.emptyGeneral: No general rules yet. Add one like “always use CTEs” or “explain your SQL” that should apply to every database.
knowledge.emptyTaught: Nothing taught yet. Add a fact like “sales lives in `customer_order`, use `fulfilled_date`” so the assistant gets it right without you repeating it. The assistant also proposes facts as you work, which show up here to Remember.
knowledge.suggested: Suggested from your chats. Remember the ones worth keeping:
knowledge.pinnedTitle: This table's columns are always included in the assistant's schema view
knowledge.placeholder: e.g. There is no sales table; sales data lives in customer_order, fulfilled_date is the sale date.
knowledge.pinTableTitle: Always include this table's columns in the assistant's schema view, even when the question doesn't mention it

audit.recordChats: Record chats with {assistant}, and every action taken on your behalf (data flows, agents)
audit.help: Each enabled kind of language-model interaction is recorded here: when it ran, which model served it, and the full exchange. Off by default; existing entries are kept until cleared. Newest first; the most recent 500 are kept.
audit.walletTitle: Your live gateway wallet (percent of the period's budget used), with the recorded turns' share to weigh against it
audit.recordedShare: recorded turns here ≈ {share} of the wallet
audit.clearBody: Every recorded language-model interaction will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
audit.empty: No interactions recorded yet. Switch recording on above and every exchange with a model lands here.
audit.shareTitle: Share of your wallet this turn used (prompt + completion)
audit.contextSent: context sent to the model (schema + what you're looking at)

privacy.intro: What the app sends us, and the switch for each. None of it carries your SQL, your results or your connection details.
privacy.official: This sends three things. When something goes wrong, a report (the error and a stack trace), scrubbed before it leaves your computer. When the app starts, an install id with its version, platform and locale. And once a day, a mark that the app was used. Once you sign in, these are linked to your account, so we can count installs and see when an account last used the app. None of it carries your SQL, query results, connection details or keys. Turning this off stops all of it.
privacy.openBuild: When something goes wrong, a report (the error and a stack trace) is sent to help us fix it. Reports are scrubbed before they leave your computer: your SQL, query results, connection details and keys are never included. A build from source sends no install or usage pings.
privacy.notConfigured: Reporting is not configured in this build, so this setting has no effect.
privacy.syncToggle: Sync my settings to my account
privacy.syncHelp: Your appearance, editor, and query preferences (theme, pane layout, and options) are saved to your account, so a new computer starts set up the way you like. Passwords, keys, and connection details are never synced; they stay encrypted on this computer.
privacy.signInToSync: Sign in to sync your settings across computers.
privacy.syncOn: Your settings will sync to your account.
privacy.syncPaused: Sync is paused on this computer.
privacy.deleteBody: This removes the copy of your preferences stored in your account. Your settings on this computer are kept, and they sync again the next time you change one.
privacy.deleted: Your synced settings were deleted from your account.
privacy.deleteFailed: Could not delete your synced settings. Please try again.

reset.intro: Choose what to clear, then Reset. Each box is independent. This cannot be undone.

items.preferencesDetail: Font size, theme, keyword case, auto-LIMIT, and the other Appearance/Editor options.
items.connectionsDetail: Deletes every saved connection along with its stored passwords and SSH keys.
items.queriesDetail: The run history and any named saved queries.
